extension.description: Your HTML comments are visible in DevTools. This writes them in the syntax Jinja, Django, Blade, Twig, Handlebars or EJS drops server-side - and converts the ones already in your code.
cmd.scanFile: Check exposed comments in this file
cmd.scanWorkspace: Check exposed comments in the project
cmd.convertFile: Convert exposed comments in this file
cmd.convertWorkspace: Convert exposed comments in the project
config.enabled: Turns the whole extension on or off.
config.showGhostComments: Shows comments stored outside the file as ghost text in the editor.
config.language.auto: Follow the VS Code display language
config.sidecarDirectory: Folder where comments that cannot live in the source file are stored.
config.contexts: Forces a context per glob pattern, e.g. { "**/*.html": "jinja" }. Valid values: jinja, blade, twig, handlebars, ejs, pug, sass, php, python, cstyle-server, hash-server, html, css, javascript, jsx, vue.
config.trustBuildForSourceMaps: Treats JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX and Vue as safe. Only turn this on if your build minifies AND publishes no source map - otherwise the comment is visible in DevTools.
config.diagnosticsSeverity: Severity of the warning about comments that reach the browser.
config.author: Name shown next to comments. Defaults to your system user.
view.welcome:
No hidden comments in this project yet.

Hidden comments are the ones stored outside the source file, for file types that have no comment syntax the browser drops.

[Add hidden comment](command:hiddenComments.add)

Comments already written in the file (such as {# ... #}) are normal code and are not listed here.
view.exposedWelcome:
Nothing exposed to the browser in this project.

This panel lists comments written in a syntax that is served to the browser, when the file type has a safer one available.

[Scan the project](command:hiddenComments.refreshExposed)
